analysis_unit.notes: Pooled corpus of positive and negative free-text comments about the Pink report style across multiple oncology scenarios; treated as an aggregated report-type subset rather than a single speaker narrative.

summary.overall_impression: This subset was viewed as evidence-rich and often appreciated for its top-line summary, explicit recommendation, and attempt to organize supporting studies by evidence level. At the same time, the dominant criticism was that the report was too long, too table-heavy, and poorly matched to point-of-care decision-making. Many comments suggest that clinicians saw value in the underlying content, but felt the presentation diluted usability by overwhelming them with dense tables, excessive citation material, and insufficient synthesis around the specific patient question. The strongest improvement signal was not to remove evidence, but to condense, better vet, and more clearly interpret it for clinical use.
dominant_positive_themes: Strong evidence orientation with study details and ranking
dominant_negative_themes: Overly long, dense, and table-heavy presentation
Poor workflow fit and limited synthesis for the clinical question
dominant_improvement_requests: Condense the table and simplify the format
Provide stronger synthesis tied to the patient-specific clinical question
Improve citation usability and vet evidence quality more carefully

positive_features.description: Many comments praised the opening summary paragraph or top-line section for quickly conveying the main point before the detailed evidence listing.
representative_examples: strong summary section
clear introductory summary
good top line summary

positive_features.description: Clinicians often valued that the report pulled together substantial literature and presented a broad overview of the evidence base.
representative_examples: fairly comprehensive summary of the data
great summary of evidence
comprehensive literature review

positive_features.description: A recurring positive feature was the attempt to rank or label evidence strength, which helped some readers orient to study quality.
representative_examples: liked ranking of citations
ranking level of evidence
order of evidence strength

positive_features.feature_label: Direct recommendation backed by supporting data
positive_features.description: Several comments appreciated that the report took a stance or offered a recommendation while still presenting supporting references.
representative_examples: clear recommendations, trial data faithfully represented
liked level of evidence and direct conclusions made from reference
supporting data present to back up this stance

positive_features.feature_label: Table can aid quick evidence lookup for some users
positive_features.description: Although the table format was the most criticized element overall, a subset of respondents found it useful as a structured reference when reviewing studies.
representative_examples: table format makes review of data easier
chart with evidence is a good idea
lists the data itself and the results, super helpful

positive_features.feature_label: Concrete study details and quoted evidence
positive_features.description: Some comments valued the inclusion of specific study numbers, primary sources, and quoted evidence rather than vague narrative statements alone.
representative_examples: included specific numbers from the studies
includes primary sources
like the evidence quoted

negative_features.description: The most consistent criticism was that the report was too long, too dense, and overloaded with material, making it hard to use in practice.
representative_examples: giant table is awful
too long
overwhelming amount of information

negative_features.description: The tabular presentation was repeatedly described as visually unappealing, cluttered, and difficult to skim because of too many rows, columns, and sections.
representative_examples: really dislike this tabular format
too many rows/columns
reference table appears messy

negative_features.description: Many respondents felt the report assembled evidence but did not synthesize it enough into a practical answer to the actual clinical question.
representative_examples: misses the clinical question entirely
doesn't synthesize the information to help with clinical decision making
just provide evidence but doesn't help summarizing the recommendations

negative_features.description: Some comments noted that the report did not adequately address patient-specific factors, clinical nuance, next steps, or uncertainty relevant to the case.
representative_examples: no individualized patient approach
not enough discussion about nuances and next steps
does not consider the patient nuances as much

negative_features.description: Respondents often wanted more usable citations, including clearer linkage, more specific references, and less cumbersome reference presentation.
representative_examples: needs specific citations for later reference
sources not hyperlinked
prefer links to ensure accurate citations

negative_features.description: A subset of comments raised concerns about inclusion of low-quality or irrelevant studies and inaccurate labeling of evidence strength.
representative_examples: inclusion of probably lower quality studies
irrelevant animal model study
narrative review isn't really a meta analysis

negative_features.description: Beyond length alone, clinicians described the report as hard to read, poorly organized, and not well designed for rapid comprehension.
representative_examples: not well organized or visually appealing
difficult to read
too many columns to skim through

negative_features.description: Some respondents were uneasy with the decisiveness of the recommendation or felt uncertainty was not adequately expressed.
representative_examples: questioned the definitive conclusion
underreport the uncertainties of treatment
need confidence when recommending

improvement_requests.request_label: Condense and simplify the table format
improvement_requests.description: Clinicians wanted a shorter, cleaner structure with fewer columns, fewer unnecessary fields, and less visual clutter.
representative_examples: too long, table too long, too many columns
simple table helps but this has too many rows/columns
would benefit from better structure
improvement_requests.targeted_problem: Information overload, poor readability, and weak workflow fit caused by the current table-heavy presentation.

improvement_requests.description: Respondents wanted the report to more clearly answer the case-specific question, summarize implications, and state what the evidence means clinically.
representative_examples: there should be a summarizing statement toward the end
needed to synthesize data after table
help summarizing the recommendations
improvement_requests.targeted_problem: The report presents evidence but often fails to translate it into a concise, decision-supportive interpretation.

improvement_requests.description: A common request was to make citations easier to use by hyperlinking, numbering, or otherwise linking in-text claims directly to references.
representative_examples: change citations to hyperlink numbers
citations not linked
would be helpful if citations in text linked directly
improvement_requests.targeted_problem: Citations are cumbersome to navigate and do not adequately support quick reference or verification.

improvement_requests.request_label: Vet and rank evidence more rigorously
improvement_requests.description: Participants wanted more careful source selection, clearer ordering by trial quality, and less inclusion of low-value or irrelevant evidence.
representative_examples: ordering should reflect the quality of the evidence
would be more beneficial if there was more vetting of the actual sources
RCTs would be presented first
improvement_requests.targeted_problem: Concerns about evidence quality, relevance, and accuracy of evidence-level labeling.

improvement_requests.request_label: Tailor the report more to the patient and decision context
improvement_requests.description: Some comments asked for greater attention to patient-specific nuance, practical next steps, and uncertainties affecting management.
representative_examples: no individualized patient approach
needed discussion of nuances and next steps
express uncertainty for clinical decision making
improvement_requests.targeted_problem: The report can feel generic and insufficiently adapted to real-world clinical decision needs.

improvement_requests.request_label: Preserve the top summary but trim the back-end detail
improvement_requests.description: The preferred direction was often not to discard the summary-plus-evidence concept, but to keep the concise opening and substantially reduce the volume of supporting material.
representative_examples: only helpful part is the one paragraph at the beginning
starting out with a summary is ideal, but five pages of references is unnecessary
summary paragraph at the top is concise
improvement_requests.targeted_problem: The current balance between overview and supporting detail is skewed too heavily toward exhaustive documentation.

mixed_or_tradeoff_comments.theme_label: Helpful evidence table versus unusable bulk
mixed_or_tradeoff_comments.description: The table format generated a clear split: some found it useful for structured evidence review, while many felt the same feature became overwhelming when expanded too far.
representative_examples: table is helpful but has to be used appropriately

mixed_or_tradeoff_comments.theme_label: Appreciated decisiveness versus discomfort with over-direction
mixed_or_tradeoff_comments.description: Some clinicians liked that the report took a stance, but others were uneasy when the recommendation seemed too definitive or directive.
representative_examples: like that there was a stance, but not sure I like when the report tells me exactly what to do

mixed_or_tradeoff_comments.theme_label: Comprehensive review versus poor point-of-care fit
mixed_or_tradeoff_comments.description: A number of comments imply the report may be useful for deeper review, research preparation, or refresher reading, but less suited to in-the-moment clinical workflow.
representative_examples: useful if I wanted to explore the data in more depth

interpretive_notes: The corpus suggests a recurring pattern of liking the underlying evidentiary ambition but rejecting the current delivery format.
Praise often focused on the opening summary, evidence ranking, and presence of supporting studies, while criticism concentrated on length, clutter, and inadequate synthesis.
This subset appears to be strongest when functioning as a literature repository and weakest when functioning as a concise clinical decision-support output.
The most actionable design implication is to preserve the summary-plus-evidence architecture while sharply reducing visual and citation burden and strengthening case-specific interpretation.
data_quality_notes: Comments are brief, fragmented, and sometimes combine praise with criticism in the same sentence.
There is redundancy around length and table-format complaints, which strengthens salience but limits conceptual breadth.
A small number of rows contain minimal or null content, and some positive comments still include embedded criticism.
